MISSOURI PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION


        CASE NO. ER-2026-0143




       REBUTTAL TESTIMONY

                  OF

      ROBERT HOLLINSWORTH

           ON BEHALF OF

     EVERGY MISSOURI METRO




          Kansas City, Missouri
              August 2026
                                     REBUTTAL TESTIMONY

                                                 OF

                                   ROBERT HOLLINSWORTH


                                     CASE NO. ER-2026-0143

 1   Q.   Please state your name and business address.

 2   A.   My name is Robert Hollinsworth. My business address is 26486 E. 2200 Road, La Cygne,

 3        Kansas.

 4   Q.   By whom and in what capacity are you employed?

 5   A.   I am employed by Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. and serve as Senior Director Generation for

 6        Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. d/b/a as Evergy Missouri Metro (“Evergy Missouri Metro,”

 7        “EMM,” or the “Company”), Evergy Missouri West, Inc. d/b/a Evergy Missouri West

 8        (“Evergy Missouri West”), Evergy Metro, Inc. d/b/a Evergy Kansas Metro (“Evergy

 9        Kansas Metro”), and Evergy Kansas Central, Inc. and Evergy South, Inc., collectively d/b/a

10        as Evergy Kansas Central (“Evergy Kansas Central”) the operating utilities of Evergy, Inc.

11        (“Evergy”).

12   Q.   On whose behalf are you testifying?

13   A.   I am testifying on behalf of Evergy Missouri Metro.

14   Q.   What are your responsibilities?

15   A.   I currently manage La Cygne and Hawthorn Generating Stations.

16   Q.   Please describe your education, experience, and employment history.

17   A.   I hold a BS in Mechanical Engineering from Missouri Science and Technology and a MS

18        in Engineering Management from Missouri Science and Technology.              I have been




                                                    1
  1        employed by Evergy for 20 years holding numerous positions in engineering and

 2        maintenance and operations.

 3   Q.   Have you previously testified in a proceeding at the Missouri Public Service

 4        Commission (“MPSC” or “Commission”) or before any other utility regulatory

 5        agency?

 6   A.   No.

 7   Q.   What is the purpose of your testimony?

 8   A.   The purpose of my rebuttal testimony is to respond to Staff witness Young’s assertion that

 9        certain generation assets were retired before the end of their average book life. See the

10        Rebuttal testimony of Ron Klote, Ryan Mulvany, and Darrin Ives for additional

11        information to rebut Staff’s adjustment.

12   Q.   Do you agree with Staff’s characterization of these projects as improper early

13        retirements?

14   A.   No. There are many factors that drive the need to replace infrastructure. Below I explain

15        examples from Staff Data Request No. 191 to illustrate the types of operational factors that

16        can drive replacement before the end of the average asset group useful life.

17              Boiler superheater sections retired due to recurring material failures (Iatan

18               Unit 2, Work Order 10001198; La Cygne Unit 2, Work Order 10002398; and

19               Hawthorn Unit 5, Work Order 10002198). The largest dollar amount of

20               retirements on Staff's list involves major boiler heating sections, known as

21               superheaters, which were retired because of recurring material failures in their tubes

22               that could not be resolved through continued monitoring or repair. At Iatan Unit 2,

23               two of these sections, both installed in 2010, experienced a recurring condition in



                                                     2
  1   which internal scale formed inside the tubes and flaked off, restricting steam flow

 2   and causing the tubes to overheat and fail. Each failure forced the unit offline — in

 3   some instances for as long as three weeks, and for nearly five consecutive weeks in

 4   early 2013. The Company and the boiler's original manufacturer agreed that the

 5   resulting loss of unit availability was unacceptable, and because the underlying

 6   condition could not be corrected by maintaining the existing tubes, replacement of

 7   the sections was the only durable solution. These sections were therefore retired

 8   because of recurring material failures, not because of their age.

 9          The La Cygne Unit 2 secondary superheater (SSH) outlet bank was retired

10   for the same reason: Approximately eight months after being installed the Unit 2

11   SSH Outlet banks experienced a large and widespread exfoliation event from the

12   stainless-steel tubing which led to numerous blocked and overheated circuits and

13   resulted in nine separate forced outages. Inspection testing indicated that roughly

14   15% of its tubes were projected to reach the end of their service life far earlier than

15   would be expected for their age.

16          Hawthorn Unit 5's superheater outlet tubes were replaced due to high

17   temperature creep: its tubes were failing after extended service in the high-

18   temperatures common in the final stage of boiler superheaters. Inspection testing

19   identified a number of tubes with little to no remaining service life, confirming that

20   the section was reaching the end of its usable life and would continue to fail if left

21   in service. In each of these cases, the equipment was retired because it was

22   experiencing recurring failures that testing confirmed would continue, which is

23   precisely why it could not remain in service to reach the average useful life.



                                         3
  1               Equipment retired because its condition no longer supported safe and reliable

 2                operation (Hawthorn Unit 6, Work Order 10002711; and Hawthorn Unit 5,

 3                Work Order 10001681). A second group of equipment was retired because the

 4                condition had reached a point where continued operation would have created a

 5                significant risk of a larger and more costly failure. In the Hawthorn Unit 6 gas

 6                turbine, the blades and vanes located in the hottest section of the machine gradually

 7                degrade under extreme heat and reach a required replacement point measured by

 8                hours of operation. They must be retired at that point, rather than operated longer,

 9                because a degraded blade can become dislodged during operation; if that occurs, it

10                causes extensive damage to the surrounding turbine components and can remove

11                the unit from service for up to two years while replacement parts are manufactured.

12                These components were therefore retired specifically to prevent a catastrophic in-

13                service failure, not as a discretionary upgrade.

14                        In a related project, the coal-grinding equipment on Hawthorn Unit 5 was

15                approaching the end of its service life and could no longer consistently process the

16                coal to the fineness required for proper combustion, which was affecting unit

17                performance; it was retired and replaced because it could no longer perform reliably

18                and would have required replacement in the near future in any event since the

19                equipment was nearing its end of useful life. In both cases, the basis for retirement

20                was the condition of the equipment and the risk associated with continued

21                operation, not its age on the accounting records.

22   Q.   Does that conclude your testimony?

23   A.   Yes, it does.
